cash.name: Cash
cash.title: Cash and zakat
cash.rule: What is in the till and in the bank on your day counts.

stock.name: Stock
stock.title: The value of your stock
stock.rule: What is meant for sale counts, at its value on your day.

usage.name: Things you use
usage.title: Things you use
usage.rule: Premises, vehicle, equipment and furniture do not count.

receivables.name: Receivables
receivables.title: Receivables and zakat
receivables.rule: What your customers owe you counts if it will be paid.
receivables.detail: A doubtful receivable owes nothing until it is collected; opinions differ on what is due on collection.

other.name: Other assets
other.title: Your other assets
other.rule: Add what you own on your day; you decide what counts.
other.detail: Each line has its own “Counted” switch. Mizan applies no automatic calculation to property.

debts.name: Debts
debts.title: Debts and zakat
debts.rule: Depending on your choice, all, some or none of your debts are deducted.
debts.detail: The schools differ on deducting debts. The question rests mainly on the Companions' sayings and on scholars' reasoning.

nisab.name: Threshold
nisab.title: The threshold
nisab.rule: Below it, no zakat is due.
nisab.detail: The threshold is 200 silver dirhams or 20 gold dinars. Their conversion into grams differs (595, 612 or 624 g of silver depending on the dirham weight used): Mizan shows 595 g and 85 g, the usual conversion.

rate.name: Rate and year
rate.title: The rate and the year
rate.detail: Zakat is due after a full year (hawl).

recipients.name: Recipients
recipients.title: Who receives zakat?
recipients.rule: The Quran names eight categories of recipients.

quran_2_267.text: The Quran calls on believers to give from the good things they have earned; Mujahid understands this as trade.

quran_9_60.text: The Quran reserves zakat for eight categories of recipients, named one by one.

bukhari_1454.text: In Abu Bakr's letter on zakat, silver owes a quarter of a tenth, that is 2.5%.

bukhari_1459.text: The Prophet ﷺ indicated that below five awaq of silver, no zakat is due.

bukhari_1463.text: The Prophet ﷺ indicated that the horse or servant a Muslim has for his own use owes no zakat.

abu_dawud_1562.text: Samura ibn Jundub reports that the Prophet ﷺ ordered them to pay zakat on what they intended for sale.
abu_dawud_1562.judgment: Weak according to al-Albani, good according to Ibn Abd al-Barr.

abu_dawud_1573.text: According to Ali, the Prophet ﷺ set five dirhams on two hundred held for a year, nothing on gold below twenty dinars, and no zakat before a full year.

abu_dawud_1574.text: According to Ali, the Prophet ﷺ asked for one dirham in forty on silver, a quarter of a tenth.

ibn_umar.text: Ibn Umar held that goods meant for sale are subject to zakat.
ibn_umar.judgment: Authentic chain according to Ibn Hazm and al-Nawawi.

umar_himas.text: Umar asked Himas to value his goods, then to pay zakat on them.

uthman.text: Uthman ibn Affan would urge, in the month of zakat, anyone with a debt to settle it first, then to pay zakat on what remained.

stock_schools.text: The four schools hold that goods are subject to zakat, at their value on the day; Ibn al-Mundhir reports a consensus on it.

receivables_schools.text: The schools count a sure receivable, owed by a solvent customer who acknowledges it, and differ on when to pay. A doubtful receivable owes nothing until it is collected.

jewelry_schools.text: For jewellery that is worn, the question is a matter of school opinion.

real_estate.text: A property lived in or for personal use does not count, by unanimous opinion; a property bought to resell counts like goods.

aaoifi_stock.text: The AAOIFI standard values stock at its expected realisable value; the purchase price only when the current value is unknown.

aaoifi_debts.text: The AAOIFI standard deducts only what is due within 12 months.

aaoifi_rate.text: Over a solar year, 11 days longer, the AAOIFI standard uses a rate of 2.5775%.

stock_valuation.sale: Retail price for a retailer, wholesale price for a wholesaler.
stock_valuation.purchase: Only when the current value is unknown.

receivables_mode.yearly: For the Malikis, on a regular trader's sales.

debts_mode.all: Each school sets its own conditions.

nisab_method.silver: Those who keep the threshold most favourable to the poor; Islamic Relief recommends it.
nisab_method.gold: Those who consider silver no longer reflects wealth.

home.title: Lived in or for personal use

rented.title: Rented out
rented.note: Classical opinion: the property value does not count, rent still on hand counts as cash. Contemporary opinion: treated like a harvest, 10% or 5% of the rent.

resale.title: Bought to resell
resale.note: Counted at its value on your day, like goods.
